findings.problem: JobWorkflow has no typestate enum; lifecycle is encoded as independent mutable booleans, allowing impossible state combinations like status=completed with is_sent=false and sent_at_epoch_ms=None.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct any combination of is_validated, is_sent, and status strings, including semantically illegal states that no transition function ever produces legitimately.
findings.fix: Replace the struct with a typestate enum like enum JobState { Pending { id: JobId, validated: bool }, Sent { id: JobId, validated: bool, sent_at: EpochMs } } with transitions only through named functions.

findings.problem: status is pub String, allowing arbitrary values like "sent", "invalid", "garbage", or "" that have no domain meaning and no enforced transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can set item.status to any string, bypassing the intended state machine entirely; pattern matching on status is string equality, not exhaustive enum matching.
findings.fix: Replace with enum JobStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and remove is_validated and is_sent fields, folding their meaning into enum variants.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle flags that encode partial state without ordering or transition guarantees. Two booleans cannot express a proper state machine.
findings.failure_mode: A job can be is_validated=false and is_sent=true simultaneously, or is_validated=true and is_sent=false with status="pending", representing states that the domain logic should never permit.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with typestate enum variants that encode which lifecycle stage the job has reached. Each variant owns the data it needs and nothing else.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from the lifecycle booleans. When is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms could be None (invalid: sent without timestamp). When is_sent=false, it could be Some (invalid: timestamp without sent status).
findings.failure_mode: The Option field can be in any state independent of is_sent, so the struct can represent jobs that were sent without a timestamp or have timestamps without ever being sent. This breaks audit trails and time-based queries.
findings.fix: Move sent_at into the Sent variant of a typestate enum so sent_at_epoch_ms is only present when the job is actually in the Sent state. Use a newtype for the timestamp value.

findings.problem: id is pub String with no domain semantics. Any string value is accepted, including empty strings, strings with whitespace, or strings that are not valid job identifiers.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid job IDs can be constructed at any call site without validation, and there is no compile-time guarantee that id values come from a trusted parsing boundary. Collisions and injection are possible.
findings.fix: Replace with pub id: JobId where JobId is a newtype wrapping a validated string or a UUID/ulid, constructed through a fallible smart constructor at the parse boundary.

findings.problem: JobWorkflow is constructed directly from raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) with no parse boundary or smart constructor. There is no fallible validation at any entry point, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without validation, so the core logic consumes untrusted values. External input (e.g., deserialization, API input) can create any combination of id/status/flags without checks.
findings.fix: Add a fallible smart constructor like fn new(id: &str, status: JobStatus, sent_at: Option<EpochMs>) -> Result<JobWorkflow, JobError> that validates inputs at the boundary, or replace the struct entirely with a typestate enum whose variants are constructed by named transition functions.
